text.L1: Numbers become larger as we move left through place values.
text.L2: A comma is not decorative. In the Indian system, its position follows a fixed pattern.
text.L3: Each place is ten times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and lakhs.
text.L4: To write one lakh seven thousand forty, place the digits as 1, 0, 7, 0, 4, 0.
text.L5: The zeros hold empty places, so the number is 1,07,040, not a shorter number.
text.L6: First put a comma after three digits from the right, then after every two digits.
text.L7: A number with more digits is bigger; 1,00,000 is the smallest six-digit number and is ten times 10,000.
text.L8: Now choose the correct Indian comma pattern for 125000.
